Clara Nogueira here. My working day used to be very different. I used to start at nine and finish at six. I used to carry one diary in my pocket, and it used to be enough. I used to work only on domestic cases. Now my first message arrives at five in the morning, from Singapore, and the last one at eleven at night, from Chicago. My caseload used to be thirty-one cases. Today it is fourteen, and it is heavier.

Eduardo, Tom Baker. Thirty years ago this job used to be much simpler. A commodity lawyer in Brazil used to work in one legal system. He used to read one contract a week, and it used to be in Portuguese. We used to send documents by fax, and we used to wait three days for an answer. That job does not exist now. Today the same lawyer works with three legal systems, and he answers in three hours. I started at forty-one.
